subject: Non-learning commitment and data sovereignty checks for CuraSync pilot
messages:
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@curasync.health>
To: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: michael.liu@curasync.health
Date: 2027-10-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot: request for no-training commitment + provenance evidence

Hi Hannah (and Marissa),

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency profile looked promising for our triage flows. Before we greenlight the pilot we need to confirm two items in writing: a narrow no-training / no-derivatives commitment for pilot data, and an operational proof that data will not leave our requested geography or be used for model improvement.

Specifically CuraSync needs:
- A written statement that data submitted during the pilot will not be used to train or improve any models (no-training).
- A list of subprocessors that will have access to any tenant data, and the residency/region for each (we need to ensure EU/US separation for some records).
- A short evidence artifact (ops checklist or screenshot) showing ephemeral KV/prefix caching behavior and where logs are stored/how long.

If you can provide a short template or matrix we can include with our security review. We have a standard DPA redline and I can send that after your reply — would appreciate high-level commitments up-front so our legal/security teams know whether this is feasible.

Thanks — Ellen

--

Subject: Re: Pilot: request for no-training commitment + provenance evidence

Hannah / team — attaching the subprocessor inventory (subprocessor_inventory_2027Q3.csv) and summarizing the operational points we can provide to CuraSync. Below is copy we recommend for the pilot addendum and the short ops evidence outline.

Recommended pilot language (suggested DPA addendum, 2 sentences):
"For the duration of the CuraSync pilot (the 'Pilot Period'), Redwood Inference will not use Customer Pilot Data to train, tune, or improve any machine learning models or derivative models. Redwood will not assert any ownership over Customer Prompt/Response outputs created during the Pilot Period; all outputs produced from Customer Pilot Data remain the property of the Customer."

Operational evidence (one-page ops summary):
- Subprocessors: Only the listed subprocessors in attached CSV will have access; primary inference and logging run in Redwood-managed clusters in the customer's requested region (us-west-2).
- KV/prefix cache: caching is ephemeral per-tenant; TTL defaults to 0 for pilot mode and KV entries are never persisted to training stores.
- Telemetry/logs: request logs are stored in a region-tagged S3 bucket with 90-day retention for pilot; access is audited and restricted.
- Training pipeline isolation: model training pipelines run in separate clusters and do not mount live inference telemetry; ingestion to training stores is gated by an approval workflow and requires explicit label and export job.

Attachments: subprocessor_inventory_2027Q3.csv (columns: name, role, region, contract_link), proof_matrix_template.xlsx (ops checklist).

Notes for Legal (Kim): if the customer requires contractual 'no-derivatives' vs 'no-training' language, we can add clarifying phrases about derivatives and export rights. Also flagging: customer may request KMS-onshore or an on-prem connector for full data residency — that will move this to a Dedicated/Private conversation.

Happy to stand up a short call with CuraSync's security team if they want a live run of the ops evidence (I can share screens).

-David

--
David Kim

Redwood Inference
